stories.title: Oktoberfest 2026: How A Royal Wedding Gave Birth To The World's Famous Beer Festival - News18
stories.normalizedTitle: oktoberfest 2026 how royal wedding gave birth world s famous beer festival news18
stories.editorialSummary: Oktoberfest’s origins lie in the celebrations held in Munich for the marriage of Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria and Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen in October 1810. A public horse race organised for the royal wedding later became the foundation of the annual festival, which evolved into one of the world’s best-known beer and cultural events. ([muenchen.de](https://www.muenchen.de/en/events/oktoberfest?utm_source=openai))
brief: The first celebration took place in 1810 after the royal wedding of Ludwig and Therese. The festivities included a horse race attended by members of the royal family and the people of Bavaria. ([muenchen.de](https://www.muenchen.de/en/events/oktoberfest?utm_source=openai))

The event was repeated in later years and gradually developed into a regular Munich festival. The grounds came to be known as Theresienwiese, or Therese’s meadow, in honour of the bride. ([stadt.muenchen.de](https://stadt.muenchen.de/infos/stadtgeschichte.html?utm_source=openai))

Although Oktoberfest is now strongly associated with beer, its beginnings were linked to a royal wedding, public celebrations and horse racing. Over time, food, music, traditional clothing and large beer tents became central parts of the festival’s identity. ([oktoberfest.de](https://www.oktoberfest.de/en/magazine/tradition/the-history-of-oktoberfest?utm_source=openai))
keyPoints: Oktoberfest began in Munich in 1810 as part of celebrations for a royal wedding. ([muenchen.de](https://www.muenchen.de/en/events/oktoberfest?utm_source=openai))

The first event featured a horse race rather than beginning as a modern beer festival. ([muenchen.de](https://www.muenchen.de/veranstaltungen/oktoberfest/geschichte-des-oktoberfests-ereignisse-und-historische-fotos?utm_source=openai))
The festival venue, Theresienwiese, takes its name from Princess Therese. ([oktoberfest.de](https://www.oktoberfest.de/en/information/getting-there/where-is-the-oktoberfest?utm_source=openai))

stories.title: Gondhal Director's 'Priority Was To Make Film Internationally', Wanted To Show India Beyond 'Poverty, Caste - News18
stories.normalizedTitle: gondhal director s priority was make film internationally wanted show india beyond poverty caste news18
stories.editorialSummary: Marathi filmmaker Santosh Davakhar says his film “Gondhal” was conceived for international audiences while seeking to present India through its cultural heritage and traditions. The film, a mystery thriller with ritual elements, has been selected as India’s official entry for the Oscars. ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/i-didnt-know-if-people-will-like-this-film-or-not-gondhal-director-santosh-davakhar-on-oscars-entry/articleshow/134347901.cms?utm_source=openai))
brief: Davakhar said his approach was shaped by his observations at international film festivals, where he felt Indian cinema was often viewed through themes such as poverty and caste-based inequality. His stated aim was to offer a broader cultural representation of the country without denying the importance of those social realities. ([thehawk.in](https://www.thehawk.in/news/showbiz/gondhal-director-santosh-davakhar-wanted-to-move-beyond-pov-of-indian-cinema-being-about-poverty-casteism?utm_source=openai))

The director described “Gondhal” as a film that combines mystery-driven storytelling with Indian rituals and cultural traditions. He also said that extensive screenplay research and exposure to international cinema influenced the film’s structure and presentation. ([nationpress.com](https://www.nationpress.com/entertainment/gondhal-director-on-indias-oscar-push?utm_source=openai))

The film’s selection as India’s official Oscar entry places a Marathi-language production in the international awards spotlight. Davakhar has said he wanted the work to communicate across borders while retaining its Indian identity. ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/i-didnt-know-if-people-will-like-this-film-or-not-gondhal-director-santosh-davakhar-on-oscars-entry/articleshow/134347901.cms?utm_source=openai))
keyPoints: Santosh Davakhar directed the Marathi film “Gondhal.” ([timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/i-didnt-know-if-people-will-like-this-film-or-not-gondhal-director-santosh-davakhar-on-oscars-entry/articleshow/134347901.cms?utm_source=openai))

The filmmaker said he wanted to present India’s cultural heritage to international audiences alongside, rather than only through, familiar social themes. ([thehawk.in](https://www.thehawk.in/news/showbiz/gondhal-director-santosh-davakhar-wanted-to-move-beyond-pov-of-indian-cinema-being-about-poverty-casteism?utm_source=openai))

“Gondhal” has been selected as India’s official entry for the Oscars and blends thriller elements with rituals and cultural traditions. ([nationpress.com](https://www.nationpress.com/entertainment/gondhal-director-on-indias-oscar-push?utm_source=openai))
